learningObjectives.title: Other forms of worship and du'a

questions.q: How many times a day are Muslims required to perform Salah?
questions.explain: Salah is performed five times a day: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

questions.q: What is the name of the ritual washing performed before Salah?
questions.explain: Wudu is the ritual ablution using water to purify the body before prayer.

questions.q: Which direction must Muslims face when performing Salah?
questions.explain: Muslims face the Qiblah, the direction of the Ka'bah in Makkah, during prayer.

questions.q: Which prayer is performed at dawn?
questions.explain: Fajr is the first of the five daily prayers, performed at dawn before sunrise.

questions.q: What is the Muslim call to prayer known as?
questions.explain: The adhan is the call to prayer, traditionally called out by the muezzin.

questions.q: What is a rak'ah in Salah?
options: A single unit of prescribed movements and recitations
The prayer mat used during worship
questions.explain: A rak'ah is one complete cycle of standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting with set recitations.

questions.q: Why do Muslims perform wudu before Salah?
options: To achieve ritual purity before standing before Allah
To keep warm before entering the mosque
To signal the start of Ramadan
questions.explain: Wudu places the worshipper in a state of ritual and physical cleanliness fit for prayer.

questions.q: What is the significance of the position of sujud (prostration) in Salah?
options: It shows complete humility and submission to Allah
It marks the end of the fast
It is a greeting to other worshippers
It is only performed during Hajj
questions.explain: In sujud the forehead touches the ground, expressing total submission and humility before Allah.

questions.q: A Muslim hears the adhan for Zuhr while at work far from a mosque. What may he do?
options: Perform the prayer on a clean surface facing the Qiblah
Skip the prayer until he returns home in the evening
Combine all five prayers into the Isha prayer
Wait until Friday to pray at the mosque
questions.explain: Salah may be offered on any clean spot, such as a prayer mat, as long as the worshipper faces the Qiblah.

questions.q: It is Friday midday and a Muslim goes to the mosque for congregational prayer. Which prayer is this?
questions.explain: Jumu'ah is the Friday congregational prayer held at midday, including a sermon (khutbah).

questions.q: What does the Arabic word 'masjid' literally mean?
questions.explain: Masjid, the word for mosque, means 'place of prostration', reflecting the act of sujud.

questions.q: What is the mihrab in a mosque?
options: A niche in the wall showing the direction of Makkah
The tower from which the adhan is called
The dome above the prayer hall
questions.explain: The mihrab is a niche set into the qiblah wall that indicates the direction of the Ka'bah.

questions.q: What is the minbar used for?
questions.explain: The minbar is the raised pulpit from which the imam delivers the Friday sermon.

questions.q: From which feature of the mosque is the adhan traditionally called?
questions.explain: The minaret is the tower from which the muezzin traditionally calls the faithful to prayer.

questions.q: Why are there no statues or pictures of living beings in a mosque?
options: To avoid idolatry and keep worship focused on Allah alone
Because they are too expensive to produce
Because only the imam is permitted to see them
Because they are kept in a separate building
questions.explain: Images of living beings are avoided to prevent idolatry, so worship is directed to Allah alone.

questions.q: What form does decoration in a mosque usually take?
questions.explain: Mosques are decorated with Arabic calligraphy and geometric or arabesque patterns rather than figures.

questions.q: A visitor enters the prayer hall of a mosque. What is the expected practice?
options: Bring food to share during worship
Sit on a raised chair at the front
questions.explain: Shoes are removed to keep the carpeted prayer hall clean for prostration.

questions.q: What is du'a?
questions.explain: Du'a is voluntary, personal prayer or supplication that can be made at any time in any language.

questions.q: What does 'dhikr' refer to?
options: Remembrance of Allah through repeated words and phrases
questions.explain: Dhikr is the practice of remembering Allah by repeating His names and short phrases.

questions.q: How does du'a differ from Salah?
options: Du'a is voluntary and can be made anytime, while Salah is obligatory at fixed times
Du'a must be performed in Arabic, while Salah may be in any language
Du'a can only be made in a mosque, while Salah can be made anywhere
Du'a is one of the Five Pillars, while Salah is not
questions.explain: Salah is a compulsory pillar with set times and form, whereas du'a is free, personal and voluntary.
